transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-10-14
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Priya Desai (Redwood AE), Marco Chen (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Nimbus ML Lead), Tom Rivera (Nimbus CTO), Lena Ortiz (Nimbus DevOps)
Record ID: ff-20281014-nimbus-001

Summary: short walkthrough of Redwood model catalog and how we map heuristics to bench selection. Demo of console (catalog filters, compatibility matrix), quick API example, and Optimize suggestions (batching/quant, caching). Agreement to run a Dedicated bench sprint and exchange security docs.

Topics: model catalog filtering, benchmark signals, kernel/hardware compatibility, latency vs cost tradeoffs, private/Dedicated deployment considerations, SOC2/KMS questions.

00:00 Priya (Redwood AE): "Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Priya, AE on the accounts team, and Marco here is our SE who will take the deep bench questions. Appreciate you carving time. Aisha, want to kick off with a bit on what you're trying to solve?"

00:12 Aisha (Nimbus): "Yeah thanks. Uh, main thing for us is — we've got a recommendation microservice that needs sub-100ms tail latency for causal inference on single-item ranking, but cost is also a huge driver. We're evaluating open models because of licensing and flexibility. So we want to see how Redwood helps pick models + map to hardware, and then run bench runs that reflect our QPS and tail latency needs."

00:35 Tom (Nimbus): "And timeline — Q4 decision ideally. Also security: SSO + KMS + audit logs — we'll need to see those docs."

00:45 Marco (Redwood SE): "Great. High-level plan for today: catalog filters to shortlist candidates, our heuristic signals that drive bench selection (latency, tokenization, memory footprint, quantizability), compatibility matrix mapping kernels/hardware, then a short API demo showing how you'd call a shortlisted model and interpret perf stats. Finally, Optimize suggestions — batching, prefix/KV caching, quant profiles. We'll leave time for questions and then capture next steps."

01:10 Priya: "First, quick console tour. (screen share) On the catalog page you can filter by architecture, sequence length profile, quant friendly, and confidence delta. We'll add a saved view for Nimbus after the call."

02:03 Marco: "A note on the heuristics — we score models (roughly) on three axes: runtime cost per token, expected tail latency at given batch sizes, and accuracy deltas on your eval set. For open models we also tag quantization friendliness and kernel availability — e.g., some models map nicely to our 8-bit kernels on A100/MI300, others need FP16 for quality."

02:37 Aisha: "When you say kernel availability, do you mean specific low-level ops? Like does it matter if attention is flash-attn compatible?"

02:45 Marco: "Yes exactly. Flash-attn or attention variants change memory/latency. Our compatibility matrix lists which optimized kernels are available for a model architecture and which hardware they map to. It's not perfect; sometimes the auto-detection hits a false positive — transcription note: we sometimes call it 'kernel map' or 'kernel match'."

03:12 Priya: "Also worth noting we expose these heuristics in the API - so you can programmatically pull candidate lists for CI and trigger bench jobs."

03:28 Aisha: "Can I see an example of a bench selection? Like you said, heuristics -> bench priority."

03:32 Marco: "Yeah — let me pull up the bench picker. (screen) Here we have your workload profile: avg sequence 48 tokens, 95th pct length 120, target qps 150, p95 latency target 90ms. Heuristics score candidates: cost score, latency risk, and quant risk. The top candidate in this view is 'open-ld-3-small' (placeholder), second is 'alti-7b' — but note the bench payoff: alti-7b quantizes well so cost drops 40% on the same hardware but has a 2-3% quality delta on our eval slice."

04:10 Aisha: "Quality delta — how do you measure that? We have a proprietary ranking eval set; can we plug that in?"

04:18 Marco: "Yes. We can run your eval set during the benchmark sprint. In the console you can upload a small prompt set or link an S3 bucket. That will be used for accuracy deltas and for regression alerts. We'll also show you how to pin model versions and roll back if quality drops."

04:45 Tom: "Security quick question — if we run Dedicated, does data ever leave our VPC? We need to confirm encryption at rest and KMS integration."

04:54 Priya: "Good question. For Redwood Dedicated/Private deployments, the inference plane is inside your VPC; logs and artifacts can be optionally stored in your S3, and you can provide your KMS. We'll send the SOC2 summary and VPC deployment guide after this call. (note: sometimes we say 'SAML KMS' but it's SSO + KMS)"

05:20 Lena (Nimbus): "From infra side, we'll need an example terraform module or deployment pattern for the Dedicated setup — and network egress requirements."

05:31 Marco: "We have a terraform starter and sample firewall rules. I'll attach the runbook. Also, in Dedicated you can pick GPU types and we show you the estimated token/sec per GPU and cost per 1M tokens in the console. That helps choose A100 vs MI300 vs cheaper T4-like instances for emb/short ctx workloads."

06:04 Priya: "Back to the API — quick demo of a generation call. (typing) Simple JSON: model: 'open-ld-3-q8', input: prompt, streaming true. In the response we include token-level timing and model_variant info so you can see if a fallback had to occur — e.g., we failed over to a lower-memory variant during spikes."

06:40 Aisha: "Fallbacks — can we control the policy? I don't want a lower-quality fallback to be used without an alert."

06:46 Marco: "Yes — rollout policies in the console let you set thresholds and automatic rollback. You can require manual approval for fallback to different model families. Also we'll emit events into your event sink for every fallback so you can alert."

07:05 Tom: "What about hybrid routing — say we want low-latency on US-East but cheaper batch in US-West, can Redwood route by region?"

07:14 Priya: "Yes: smart routing. You can set policies by latency SLO or cost budget. We also support weight-based A/B routing for experiments."

07:30 Aisha: "Show me the compatibility matrix page — I want to understand kernel-level mismatches."

07:34 Marco: "(screen) Here: rows are models, columns are kernel/ops: flash-attn, rotary variants, custom fused kernels, quant profile availability. Green means tested in our infra; yellow means we have a best-effort patch; red means we haven't validated. There's also a notes column — e.g., 'requires sequence-splitting for >2k tokens'. Sometimes model metadata is noisy so human review in play for final bench shortlist."

08:20 Lena: "You mentioned quant profiles — do you handle 8-bit dynamic quant vs static quant? Which do you recommend?"

08:28 Marco: "We support multiple quant profiles. For many of the ranking workloads, 8-bit dynamic (QAT-lite style) gives best cost/latency tradeoff with small quality delta. The console will suggest a quant profile based on the model tag and your eval signal. We also surface a 'quant risk' score where higher means test-first."

08:52 Aisha: "Okay, let's talk bench logistics. What's included in the Sprint?"

08:57 Marco: "A typical 2-4 hour sprint includes deploy of the candidate model variants on Dedicated or a Redwood-hosted bench cluster, run of your eval and production-like QPS distribution (we mimic spikes), collect p50/p95/p99 latency and token/sec, and generate a bench report with recommended final model + quant profile + cost estimate. We'll also run a fallback / failover simulation."

09:28 Priya: "We'll attach a sample bench report from a previous customer so you can see the format. Deck and bench sheet links: Deck: https://redwood.ai/decks/catalog-pathfinder (shared) ; Bench sheet: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/nimbus-bench (placeholder)"

09:50 Tom: "When do you expect bench results? If we schedule the sprint week of 10/23, can we have results in 3 days?"

09:58 Marco: "Yes, typically 48-72 hours after the sprint for the initial report. If we need deeper kernel work it can take longer — we'll flag that upfront."

10:10 Aisha: "Cost — can you show an example projection?"

10:15 Marco: "(screen) We have a cost estimator where you input token volumes and quant profile. Example: for 150 QPS with 48 avg tokens, open-ld-3 with q8 on A100 came to $0.18 per 1k requests; alti-7b q8 on MI300 was $0.12 per 1k requests but with noted quality delta. These are example numbers; actuals depend on commit/Reserved vs on-demand Dedicated pricing."

10:46 Lena: "Do you provide autoscaling recommendations? We have variable traffic — peak windows up to 3x baseline."

10:52 Priya: "Yes, Dedicated supports autoscaling policies and burst pools. Our Optimize module will recommend scaling thresholds and batch targets so you don't overprovision but maintain latency SLOs. We'll also show token-level cost breakdowns in the Console."

11:12 Aisha: "Edge case: we have some PII that must never touch third-party storage. If we run Hosted, can we ensure data is not logged?"

11:20 Priya: "We support no-logging policies and redaction on the Hosted API, but for strict PII requirements Dedicated/Private is recommended so you control all storage. We'll include this in the security docs."

11:36 Tom: "Competitors question: we've also chatted with HuggingFace Inference and a smaller infra vendor 'CloudSpin' — how would you differentiate Redwood for this use-case?"

11:46 Marco: "Short answer: we focus on production economics and the operational features — integrated benching tied to model catalog heuristics, rollout policies, and routing controls. We aim to reduce the time from shortlist to deployable baseline, and give deterministic cost/latency signals so your infra decisions are predictable."

12:10 Aisha: "One more: can we automate periodic re-bench when model versions update?"

12:16 Marco: "Yes — you can hook bench jobs to CI or schedule recurring sprints. We can auto-run evals on model catalog updates and alert if quality regresses."

12:30 Priya: "Quick Q&A before we wrap. Lena?"

12:34 Lena: "Network egress — what's outbound traffic pattern during bench? We can't open broad egress to the internet."

12:39 Marco: "Bench uses your VPC endpoints; we can provide IP ranges and also run the bench fully within your network for Dedicated. We'll include a terraform example."

12:55 Aisha: "Alright, let's summarize next steps and owners."

13:00 Priya: "Recap: 1) I'll send the tailored bench spreadsheet + cost projection and the SOC2/VPC guide (Priya) — due 10/18. 2) We'll schedule a 2-hour Dedicated benchmark sprint week of 10/23 — Marco to drive runbook. 3) Nimbus to provide eval S3 and sample traffic profile (Lena) by 10/19. 4) We'll prepare a sample terraform starter for Dedicated (Marco)."

13:28 Tom: "Sounds good. Any blockers from our side: internal sign-off for Dedicated but we'll aim to get that by the sprint date."

13:38 Priya: "Great — we'll follow up in email with calendar invites and the shared links. Thanks everyone."

13:45 (call ends)

Transcript notes: occasional mis-transcriptions: 'KV cash' for KV cache, 'alti' is a shorthand for specific model family, and 'CloudSpin' is an internal vendor name. Some timestamps approximate.
